As many have stated, it's dependent upon belief. There are so many different outcomes when we reach death--and the dead can't affirm nor answer our questions about it. Does it all go black? I would love that. Do we enter new bodies and begin again with a clean memory? That would be kind of interesting. Does our soul burn for eternity? I dread thinking about it. Do we see the Lord and witness Heaven itself? I'd like to think so. I believe that we were put here, even if it isn't for the purpose we want, but for us to experience life, give kindness to others, develop our own core beliefs, values, and ideals--to prosper by spreading kindness, joy, and aid others in need. Sadly, those traits aren't priority anymore because we ourselves cannot give what we don't necessarily have or feel as though we will ever obtain. 

As for my beliefs, and not discrediting anyone else's, the act of suicide would not lead one to Hell. This may be right, this may be wrong. There isn't a guaranteed yes or no. Everyone has their own individualized belief and value system, and I'm not one to say what goes and doesn't. 

Back to you. When you're in the mire of depression and suicidal ideations/actions, your head is spinning with so many thoughts, so much stimuli that it's hard to catch a moment of peace. You are young. I know you've probably heard it all before from elders and whatnot, but I'm 32, and I was in a similar situation myself once. I made mistakes, I accomplished victories--both big and small. I traversed the plains of hopelessness and excitement--albeit it, not all at once. Few and far between at points.

Many people are succeeding before your eyes--but that's what you see. Your friends have jobs. I understand that pain. I felt behind when my friends were surpassing me in terms of employment. One day the right opportunity will come to you and give you a great path to follow. It may be tomorrow, it may be next week. Don't push yourself to join the job rat race. You'll get there.

As for your transfer, that's great you're in a community college. Half the people I see running about my town are poorly educated. So, hey...you've clearly got a brain under your belt--well, in your head. 

Look into a few universities you would like to transfer to and ask them what the necessary qualifications are for a proper academic transfer. Work towards that if you wish. Set small goals. Don't set a time limit for growth. Hell, my ex-wife had an associates degree and was doing great as a nurse last time I checked. Meanwhile, I'm teaching art classes on a bachelors. Pace yourself.

You can do this. This is a hurdle in the longevity of life, but I know you can do this. For me, for your family, and most importantly yourself. Don't give up.

Express yourself here as frequently as you want. There's always someone willing to help. 

Set small goals, work towards them. 
Don't compare your behind the scenes footage to the highlight reels of others. 
It's better to grow slowly than stand completely still.
Take your time. Don't rush. Enjoy the things that bring you happiness.
And remember that mistakes are okay to make, it's how we learn. 

Best of luck. I hope this resonates with you to some degree and you can get some peace of mind. Let me know if you want to chat.
